security_audit.summary: The majority of static findings are false positives caused by security signatures, vulnerable examples, Markdown code blocks, and analyzer rule definitions. Confirmed risks are limited to intended filesystem modification by the auto-fix and report tools, plus a documented sudo installation command that requires explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Auto-fix and report generation can write to project files or user-selected output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before applying fixes or writing reports, display the resolved target path, and keep backup and rollback behavior enabled by default.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes a sudo package installation command.
remediation.suggestion: State that privileged installation is optional, prefer non-privileged package managers when possible, and require manual user approval before running any sudo command.

remediation.issue: Dependency scanning launches external audit tools.
remediation.suggestion: Use fixed argument arrays as implemented, never pass unsanitized user input to a shell, and ask before running package-manager audits that may access the network.

content.value_statement: Security bugs are hard to find across languages, frameworks, and dependencies. Vibe Security gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured checks, fix guidance, and reporting workflows for safer reviews.
actual_capabilities: Runs AST-based and pattern-based checks for common vulnerabilities in Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
Tracks tainted input into dangerous sinks for injection, XSS, deserialization, and path traversal review.
Suggests safer remediation patterns for SQL injection, XSS, command injection, and weak cryptography.
Scans dependency manifests with ecosystem audit tools when those tools are installed locally.
Generates HTML, JSON, CSV, and SARIF-style reports from scan results.
limitations: Results are advisory and require human security review before production changes.
Some examples and rule data can trigger static scanner false positives.
Dependency audit coverage depends on installed tools such as npm audit, pip-audit, and cargo-audit.
Auto-fix changes should be reviewed and tested before committing.

use_cases.title: Review a web application before release
use_cases.description: Scan controllers, views, and API handlers for injection, XSS, authentication, and configuration issues before deployment.

use_cases.title: Triage dependency vulnerabilities
use_cases.description: Check package manifests for known CVEs and summarize affected packages, severity, and possible fixed versions.

use_cases.title: Teach secure coding patterns
use_cases.description: Compare vulnerable examples with safer patterns for queries, output encoding, subprocess usage, and password hashing.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic security scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to scan this project for common web application vulnerabilities. Summarize critical and high issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a suspicious code path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to analyze the authentication and input handling in this feature. Trace user-controlled data to dangerous sinks and explain each risk.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest safe fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to propose fixes for these findings. Prioritize minimal safe changes, explain why each fix works, and list tests I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a release security report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to perform a release audit, include dependency scan results, map findings to OWASP and CWE, and produce a concise remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Scan my Express routes for SQL injection and XSS.
output: Recommended safer query and output encoding patterns
Follow-up tests to verify the fix
List of vulnerable packages by ecosystem
Severity and CVE identifiers when available
Notes about audit tool coverage and missing manifests

output_examples.input: Create a security report for the latest scan results.

best_practices: Run scans on a clean working tree and review every proposed file change before applying it.
Fix critical injection, authentication, and secret exposure issues before lower-severity cleanup.
Re-scan and run tests after remediation to confirm the issue is resolved.
anti_patterns: Do not run auto-fix on production files without reviewing the exact diff first.
Do not treat scanner output as proof that a system is secure.
Do not paste real secrets into prompts, examples, or scan fixtures.

faq.question: Does Vibe Security replace a professional security audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps find and explain likely issues, but human review and testing are still required.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it modify my code automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, the auto-fix tool can apply changes with backups. Review the target path and diff before approving changes.

faq.question: Does dependency scanning require internet access?
faq.answer: Some ecosystem audit tools may contact package or vulnerability services. Ask before running them in restricted environments.

faq.question: Why are there many dangerous-looking examples in the skill?
faq.answer: The skill includes vulnerability signatures and teaching examples so it can detect and explain unsafe patterns.

faq.question: What should I do after receiving findings?
faq.answer: Confirm each finding, apply the smallest safe fix, run tests, and re-scan to verify remediation.
